title: Bootstrap certification of string order in quantum spin chains
authors: Sagnik Banerjee, Haoyu Guo, Debanjan Chowdhury
abstract: The many-body bootstrap certifies ground-state properties by minimizing energy over correlators constrained only by positivity, without any variational wavefunction. Its cost, however, grows exponentially with the size of the operators involved, placing the long-range string correlators that diagnose topological phases out of reach. We overcome this by treating string operators as primary objects: bare and endpoint-dressed strings satisfy a closed operator algebra with one another and with local words, yielding a semidefinite program whose cost grows only polynomially with string length. A single computation then yields estimates of string correlators of all lengths. Rigorous two-sided bounds are obtained for each target string once the ground-state energy is pinned within a window. When benchmarked against density-matrix renormalization group computations on the cluster Ising and spin$-1$ Heisenberg chains, the method certifies the nonlocal string order of the cluster and Haldane phases directly from the Hamiltonian. Our rigorous certification of string order parameters reveal that the sharpness of the bounds is set by which operators enter the calculation, not by their length alone. By exploiting algebraic closure of strings and local words, our framework lifts spatially extended observables into polynomially tractable bootstrap variables, opening up a route to wavefunction-free certification of nonlocal order in quantum many-body systems.
summary: This paper introduces a novel 'string bootstrap' method to rigorously certify nonlocal string order parameters in quantum spin chains. By treating long-range string correlators as primary variables in a Semidefinite Program, the authors overcome the exponential cost barrier associated with traditional methods. This allows for the direct, wavefunction-free certification of topological order in complex quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of rigorously certifying nonlocal string order parameters in quantum many-body systems, which are crucial diagnostics for topological phases.
main_result: The authors developed a bootstrap method that treats string operators as primary objects, allowing the certification of nonlocal string order parameters for models like the cluster Ising and spin-1 Heisenberg chains with polynomial computational cost.
method: They formulate the problem as a Semidefinite Program (SDP) by exploiting the algebraic closure of string operators, which reduces the exponential cost barrier of traditional bootstrap methods.
model_or_system: The work applies to quantum spin chains, specifically benchmarking against the Transverse-Field Ising Model (TFIM), the Cluster Ising Model (CIM), and the spin-1 Heisenberg chain.
key_observables: Nonlocal string order parameters, including Z-strings ($\langle \prod \sigma^z angle$) and the string order parameter for CIM ($	ext{SCIM}(L)$).
important_parameters: String length ($\ell$), external field strength ($h/J$), and coupling ratios ($\lambda/J$).
main_assumptions: The tractability relies on the algebraic closure of strings and local words under canonical reduction rules, allowing the problem to be framed as a polynomial-cost SDP.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the moment matrix construction, the comparison of certified bounds (e.g., $Z$-strings, $	ext{SCIM}(L)$) across different phases, and the impact of increasing the local basis size ($d$) or refining the endpoint operators.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the limitations of standard bootstrap methods, proposes the novel string-based SDP formulation, details the algebraic closure rules, and then benchmarks the method by applying it to specific Hamiltonians (TFIM, CIM, Spin-1) to certify string order.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, rigorous, and computationally tractable framework for diagnosing topological order in quantum magnets, extending beyond the limitations of variational or purely local methods.
